title: Chapter 12: The Elegant Flirt 2
content:
Chapter 12

That brand completely hijacked Wei Wuxian’s attention. His breath hitched, wondering if his eyes were playing tricks on him, so captivated by the mark that he didn't even register the man's face. Out of nowhere, a blinding white curtain swept across his vision like sudden snowfall, splitting apart an instant later as a cerulean sword-glare surged forward, trailing bone-chilling frost.

It was Hanguang-jun’s legendary blade, Bichen.

Holy hell, it’s Lan Wangji!

Dodging blades and running for dear life was second nature to Wei Wuxian. Hitting the ground in a desperate roll, he narrowly dodged the lethal frost, even finding the leisure to casually flick away a stray leaf stuck to his hair as he scrambled clear of the Cold Spring. Bolting like a headless fly, he plowed headfirst into a squad of night-patrollers.

A hand caught his collar, barking instantly, "What’s all this sprinting about?! Running is forbidden in the Cloud Recesses!"

Spotting Lan Jingyi and the disciples, Wei Wuxian practically beamed with relief.Finally, my ticket down the mountain! Break out the disciplinary paddles and beat me out the gates!

Leaning straight into the role, he threw his hands up in theatrical guilt. "I didn't see anything! I swear I didn't see a single thing! I definitely didn't come here to sneak a peek at Hanguang-jun in the bath!"

The disciples froze, their jaws practically hitting the dirt in sheer disbelief at his suicidal audacity. To them, Hanguang-jun was an untouchable paragon, revered like a god descending from the heavens. Peeping on Hanguang-jun taking a bath?! The sheer concept was an unspeakable, unforgivable sacrilege.

Lan Sizhui’s voice cracked in sheer panic. "What? Hanguang-jun?! Hanguang-jun is in there?!"

Lan Jingyi grabbed him by the scruff, his face crimson with rage. "You shameless degenerate! Is—isthatsomething you're allowed to gawk at?!"

Striking while the iron was hot, Wei Wuxian doubled down to cement his guilt. "I didn't catch a single glimpse of Hanguang-jun with his clothes off! Not one!"

"That's literally admitting it!" Jingyi sputtered. "Still making excuses?! If you weren't peeping, what were you doing creeping around here? Look at you, covering your face like you've actually got shame!"

Wei Wuxian clamped his hands over his cheeks, whining through his fingers, "Keep your voice down, will you? Clamoring is forbidden in the Cloud Recesses, remember?"

Right in the middle of the circus, the irises parted. Draped in a loose white robe, damp hair trailing down his shoulders, Lan Wangji stepped into view. In the span of barely a few sentences, he had managed to dress himself with pristine neatness, though Bichen remained drawn in his grip. The disciples snapped into formal salutes, bowing low.

Lan Jingyi blurted out, "Hanguang-jun, this Mo Xuanyu has gone entirely too far! You only brought him back out of kindness for helping at Mo Village, but he... he—"

Wei Wuxian braced himself, convinced he was about to get kicked off the mountain once and for all.

Instead, Lan Wangji cast an unreadable, sidelong glance at him. After a beat of suffocating quiet, a sharpzhengechoed through the mist as Bichen slid smoothly into its scabbard.

"Disperse."

One quiet, unremarkable word. Yet carrying the terrifying gravity of his absolute authority, no one dared squeak a word of protest. The disciples scattered like birds.

Moving with practiced ease, Lan Wangji reached out, seized Wei Wuxian by the back of his collar, and began hauling him toward the Jingshi like luggage.

In his past life, Wei Wuxian’s height had practically mirrored Lan Wangji’s, standing barely an inch shorter; two remarkably tall, slender youths walking shoulder-to-shoulder where the difference was virtually invisible. But waking up in this stolen vessel, he was dismayed to find that while Mo Xuanyu was tall enough by ordinary standards, he came up a good two inches shorter than Lan Wangji. Dangled by his scruff, he had zero leverage to put up a fight.

Wei Wuxian stumbled along, opening his mouth to kick up a fuss, but Lan Wangji shut him down with an icy drop of his voice: "Make noise, and you will be silenced."

Getting booted off the mountain was the dream; getting hit with the Silence Spell was a nightmare. Wei Wuxian was left utterly baffled.Since when did the Lan Clan go soft on peeping toms invading a senior master's bath? How on earth is he letting this slide?!

Lan Wangji marched him into the Jingshi, dragged him straight into the inner quarters, and dropped him onto the wooden daybed with a solid, unceremonious thud.

Wei Wuxian groaned as his hip took the impact. Splayed across the cushions, he was just winding up to unleash some nauseating, overly effeminate cooing to gross the man out, but glancing up, he caught Lan Wangji staring down at him, Bichen resting in hand.

Having grown up seeing the Second Young Master Lan bound in strict ribbons and pristine, buttoned-up discipline, this sight of him—hair cascading loose, draped in a light, casual robe—was completely unprecedented. Wei Wuxian couldn't help staring for an extra second or two. The rough handling had tugged Lan Wangji’s lapel slightly ajar, exposing a sharp collarbone and, resting just below it, that dark crimson brand.

The sight hooked Wei Wuxian's eyes once more.

Long before he had ever turned his back on the world to become the Yiling Laozu, he’d carried the exact same mark over his chest.

And looking at the brand on Lan Wangji’s skin right now—its precise placement, its unmistakable curvature—it was a carbon copy of the burn he used to wear. It was impossible not to feel that sharp pang of uncanny shock.

Stranger still was the tapestry of discipline scars across Lan Wangji’s back.

Rising to fame in his youth, Lan Wangji had always been held in the highest esteem—the gold standard of righteous cultivation, the crown jewel of the Lan Clan’s pride, his every gesture upheld by clan elders across the land as the shining model for young disciples. What kind of unforgivable, catastrophic transgression could have earned him a punishment that vicious?

Over thirty lashes with a discipline whip wasn't a warning; it was meant to kill. And once carved into flesh, discipline scars never faded, permanently branded onto the victim's back so they would carry the memory of their crime to their grave.

Noticing the weight of his stare, Lan Wangji’s lashes dipped slightly. He casually pulled his lapels together, concealing his collarbone and sealing the mark away, slipping back behind his usual wall of winter frost. Right then, the heavy resonance of a temple bell rolled down from the peaks.

The rules in the Cloud Recesses were unforgiving, right down to their daily rhythm: sleep at nine, rise at five. The bell was the final curfew call.

Lan Wangji waited until the lingering hum faded into the night before turning to Wei Wuxian. "You sleep here."

Without giving him a chance to answer, Lan Wangji pivoted and vanished into the adjoining chamber, leaving Wei Wuxian slumped on the daybed, drowning in confusion.

It wasn't that he hadn't suspected Lan Wangji of seeing through his disguise. But logically, that made zero sense. Sacrificial summoning was a forbidden, closely guarded curse; barely a handful of people in the entire world even knew the ritual existed. Most ancient manuscripts that survived were missing half their pages and entirely useless, leading people to dismiss the technique as myth. Heaven only knew where Mo Xuanyu had managed to dig up the ritual that yanked Wei Wuxian back into the mortal coil. Lan Wangji couldn't possibly have identified him just from that butchered flute performance.

Besides, looking back at his previous life, he and Lan Wangji had never shared some deep, soul-stirring bond. Sure, they’d studied together, dodged death side-by-side, and traded swings in the field, but it had all been transient—flowing water slipping past fallen blooms, here and gone in a blink. Lan Wangji was bred on the strict virtue of Gusu; he was destined to be righteous and refined, practically allergic to Wei Wuxian’s brand of chaos. Wei Wuxian figured their dynamic wasn't outright hostile, but calling them friends was a stretch. Lan Wangji’s verdict on him had likely mirrored everyone else's: dangerously corrupt, lacking righteous foundation, an inevitable disaster waiting to happen.

After Wei Wuxian defected from Yunmeng Jiang to pioneer demonic cultivation, the grudge between him and Gusu Lan had only deepened, especially in those final, blood-soaked months leading to his death. If Lan Wangji were truly convinced he was the Yiling Laozu, they would’ve been tearing the room apart in a death match hours ago.

Instead, reality was proving laughably absurd: back in the day, the slightest provocation would set Lan Wangji off, yet now, no matter how shamelessly Wei Wuxian threw tantrums, Lan Wangji swallowed it whole without batting an eye. Was this supposed to be personal growth? Should he clap?

After staring at the ceiling until his eyes grew sore, Wei Wuxian rolled off the mattress, creeping into the adjoining room without making a sound.

Lan Wangji lay on his side, seemingly fast asleep. Wei Wuxian ghosted closer.

He still hadn't given up on nicking that passage jade. Just as he reached out a tentative hand, Lan Wangji’s long lashes fluttered, and his eyes opened.

Throwing caution to the wind, Wei Wuxian threw himself onto the bed!

He remembered clear as day how much Lan Wangji despised physical intimacy. In the past, brush shoulders with the man and he’d launch you through a partition wall. If Lan Wangji could toleratethis, he wasn't Lan Wangji at all—Wei Wuxian would bet his life the man had been possessed!

Wei Wuxian hovered directly over him, knees braced on either side of Lan Wangji’s waist, propping his palms flat against the wooden frame to cage the man between his arms before slowly, deliberately lowering his face. The distance between them shrank by the millimeter, so close Wei Wuxian felt his own lungs hitching, until Lan Wangji finally opened his mouth.

After a beat of heavy silence, he murmured, "Get down."

Wei Wuxian leaned into the shameless grin. "Make me."

Pale, glassy amber eyes met his at point-blank range. Lan Wangji stared back, completely unfazed, and repeated himself: "...Get down."

"No way," Wei Wuxian purred. "You told me to sleep in your room, so you should've seen this coming."

Lan Wangji held his gaze. "Are you certain you want this?"

Wei Wuxian blinked. For reasons he couldn't quite put his finger on, every instinct in his skull told him he needed to think very, very carefully before answering that.

Before his cocky smirk could fully set, a sudden wave of numbness zapped through his waist, turning his legs to jelly. His arms gave out, and he collapsed flat onto Lan Wangji’s chest.

The unfinished smirk froze awkwardly on his face. His cheek was pressed flush against the right side of Lan Wangji’s chest, his entire body locked rigid, unable to twitch a single toe. Lan Wangji’s voice drifted down from right above his ear.

It was low, dark, and gravelly, the vibration of his chest rumbling against Wei Wuxian’s cheek with every syllable:

"Then you can stay like this all night."

Wei Wuxian’s brain short-circuited. He tried desperately to wiggle, but a dull, heavy ache held his lower spine in a vice, pinning him in an excruciatingly intimate heap over an unyielding, rock-hard body.

What the hell happened to Lan Zhan over these thirteen years?!

Is this even the same guy?!

I'm not the one who took over a corpse—he definitely got possessed!

While his internal world was in full meltdown, Lan Wangji shifted slightly underneath him. Thinking the man had finally hit his limit, Wei Wuxian felt a surge of hope.

Instead, Lan Wangji casually flicked a long sleeve.

The lanterns died.
